title: probe failure-mode: prevent cascading capacity churn during region failover
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Problem: During a recent multi-region failover exercise we observed cascading capacity churn and transient 5xxs as readiness probes oscillated for pods coming up in the target region. Rapid pod restarts and immediate autoscaler triggers amplified the problem: probes flapped, the HPA scaled up aggressively, new pods hit cold KV cache misses, latency SLOs breached, and circuit breakers opened downstream.

Goal: Implement a set of defensive changes to probe behavior, autoscaler stabilization, and load-shedding coordination so that region failovers and partial network/dep degradations do not cause secondary outages or SLO regressions. We want measurable improvements in availability and reduced variability during failover while keeping recovery time acceptable.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Readiness/liveness probe flapping rate reduced by >=80% during controlled failovers as measured by probe_failure_rate metric.
2) Autoscaler churn (scale events per minute per deployment) reduced by >=70% during the same tests.
3) Multi-region failover run maintains request-success-rate SLO (p95 success >= 99.5% for control plane and runtime API) in blue/green handover test.
4) No regression in steady-state cold-start p95 latency beyond 10% compared to baseline.
5) New probe policy and autoscaler heuristics deployed behind feature flag and tested in canary namespace.
acceptance_checks: Create canary namespace and run failover script (tools/failover-runner)
One run of blue->green failover without >1% SLO breach recorded
work_done:
2026-03-01: Triage and hypothesis: probe timeouts and immediate readiness toggles caused K/V cache thrash and downstream circuit-breaker trips.
2026-03-03: Built a synthetic canary check (probe-canary) that performs a minimal end-to-end query through the runtime path including a cold-KV sample; deployed to canary namespace.
2026-03-04: Implemented probe hysteresis prototype: consecutive-success and consecutive-failure counters configurable per deployment; initial version behind feature flag ff:probe-hysteresis.
2026-03-05: Added autoscaler cooldown binding: when probe instability metric > threshold, HPA enters an extended stabilization window (cooldown_ms).
2026-03-07: Ran first controlled failover against canary namespace; collected probe metrics, autoscaler events, and SLO delta.
decisions:
1) Use hysteresis on readiness probe transitions instead of increasing probe frequency — avoids transient flip-flopping while keeping liveness aggressive to detect dead pods.
2) Tie HPA scale decisions to a 'probe_stable' signal: if probe instability > 0.05 for 1min, suppress aggressive scale-outs and prefer conservative ramping.
3) Introduce a short, progressive backoff in readiness rechecks after failures (exponential up to 30s) to avoid hot loops.
4) Make load-shedding priority-aware: cheapest short-term choice is to reject non-critical low-priority requests during region handover to preserve high-priority SLOs.
5) Deploy changes behind FF with gradual rollout and add kill-switch if error budget consumption spikes.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): deploy probe-hysteresis and probe-backoff + synthetic canary checks. Enable HPA cooldown binding. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (staged rollout): flip FF in two low-traffic regions, run automated failover script and iteratively tune thresholds. Duration: 1 week.
Phase 3 (global): enable for all regions with monitoring alerting and runbook updates. Duration: 3 days.
Phase 4: follow-up: integrate with circuit-breaker signals so downstream cbs can preemptively open and avoid cascading overload. Duration: 1 sprint.
risks:
- Too-conservative probe hysteresis delays detection of genuinely unhealthy pods leading to degraded capacity. Mitigation: keep liveness probe unchanged and monitor pod-level error rates.
- HPA suppression may under-scale under bursty traffic if thresholds mis-set. Mitigation: implement emergency override policy and use real traffic shadow testing.
- Load-shedding could impact user experience; ensure high/low priority classification is validated and telemetry recorded.
